tests.description: Timed check on Textiles and Fibres

questions.question: Explain why polycotton is used for school shirts instead of 100% cotton or 100% polyester.
questions.correctAnswer: 100% cotton: comfortable but creases badly, shrinks. 100% polyester: durable and wrinkle-free but feels clammy, does not breathe. Polycotton (typically 65/35): retains cotton's breathability, gains polyester's durability and crease resistance, ideal for school uniforms.

questions.question: Compare woven and knitted fabric constructions, explaining why each suits different garments.
questions.correctAnswer: Woven: warp + weft at 90 degrees, stable, holds shape - suits structured garments (shirts, trousers). Knitted: interlocking loops, stretchy, comfortable - suits body-hugging garments (t-shirts, socks, sportswear).

questions.question: Discuss the environmental impact of synthetic fibres compared to natural fibres.
questions.correctAnswer: Synthetic: petrochemicals (non-renewable), microplastic shedding, non-biodegradable, but durable and recyclable. Natural: renewable, biodegradable, but cotton needs vast water and pesticides. Neither is perfectly sustainable - blended fabrics are hardest to recycle.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response A sportswear company is designing a running top. Evaluate 100% cotton, 100% polyester, and a cotton-polyester blend, recommending the best choice. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: identify requirements (moisture-wicking, lightweight, quick-drying); 100% cotton - absorbs sweat, heavy when wet; 100% polyester - wicks moisture, quick-drying, retains shape; cotton-poly blend - compromise but not enough wicking. Conclude: 100% polyester (or polyester-elastane blend) for performance running wear.
